spec.title: Campaign 3 · Stage B — close: the RLM is built, and it runs
spec.p: _Written 2026-07-12 ~06:48. The capstone report for FRACTALITY-RLM-PLAN v0.1 (Campaign 3, Stage B, Option B). Normative record: the plan §9 ledger

list.item: the per-phase reports; this is the narrative the owner reads._

section.title: TL;DR
section.p: Stage B is **COMPLETE**. The mandate was Option B — the descent core plus the escalation channel, a working recursive-language-model fabric with all its patterns. Every D-C3 decision landed, the floor stayed green at every boundary, and the phase closed with the first-ever live product run of fractality: **a cold GLM boss, gated by the RLM, delegated 44.4% of eligible work (vs a 16.7% naive baseline) and drove real workers end to end.**

section.title: What Stage B built (Ф0 → Ф6)

tr.td: schema-at-seam, FileRef handoff, settings-injection, escalation round-trip — all seams green
`context_from` access-list, `output_schema` + collect-seam validation, the six-axis budget lattice
escalate), capability-class routing policy, profile class
depth-guard, `fractality gate` + decision journal, await-any, refuse-near-duplicate, availability masking, retry-on-violation, merge node
terminal `RunState::Escalated` + record + fold, exit code 5 + `escalations` inbox, `/escalate` endpoint + verb, the broker `escalate` MCP tool
MT-C3-01 pre-registered → 3 paid gated runs → 44.4% delegation, end-to-end proven

section.p: The whole loop is real: `fractality gate` decides, `spawn` opens a child packet, mission-control admits it (depth-guard, sibling invariants, cold-verifier check), a pod launches a real GLM Claude-Code worker, the worker works and writes a result, acceptance runs, `Collected` folds onto the bus, and — where the task cannot be finished here — `escalate` hands it UP the tree. Descent and ascent, both wired, both tested, both observed live.

section.title: The prediction verdicts (Ф6)

list.item: **P-C3-c (no wall-budget overrun): CONFIRMED** — the axis nobody else enforces held under fire.
**P-C3-b (schema cuts rework): INCONCLUSIVE** — the menu set no `output_schema`, so the (unit-tested) gate never fired.
**P-C3-d (a Silo task escalates): INCONCLUSIVE** — the menu had no genuinely chunk-destroying task; the bosses correctly routed rather than escalated. The channel is built; the menu didn't demand it.

section.p: The two inconclusives are **menu-design gaps, not fabric gaps** (PP-004).

section.title: The decisions that shaped Stage B (long form)

list.item: **Escalation is a terminal outcome, expressed by an MCP tool** (Ф4): the worker is `running` when it decides, so `running → escalated` is clean; a result-status exit would fight the state machine. The record climbs the `parent` edges; the run does not resume.
**Verifier-accept is a readable verdict, not a hard completion gate** (Ф5): §10.8 conservative — the verdict is first-class on the record, but it does not suspend the tree.
**The single-arm, smoke-test-first trial** (Ф6): one gated arm vs the C2 naive baseline halved the spend; run 1 proved the system ran end to end before the rest of the ≤8-session cap was committed.

**The delegation mechanism switched opencode → CC+z.ai** (mid-session, owner-prompted): headless Claude Code at the z.ai gateway — fractality's own worker mechanism. It unblocked this session's grunt delegation AND is the exact mechanism the trial arms run on. The pilot ate its own dog food, end to end.
**Worker turn caps dominated completion** — `delegated` (8) is honest, but `delegated-AND-collected` (3) trailed it purely because workers timed out at 30 turns. Config, not fabric. → PP-004.
**Two predictions unexercised** (schema gate, Silo escalation) — menu gaps. → PP-004.
**No `fractality decisions` read verb** — the gate journals decisions but nothing reads them back, so P-C3-a is a direction not a number. → PP-004.

**Worker-stop after escalate is cooperative, not enforced** (Ф4); **no tree→verifier query** (Ф5); **acceptance does not feed routing yet** (FD-5 soft-label table, off D-C3-8) — all non-blocking, all noted in their phase reports.

section.title: Strategic verdict
section.p: Stage B set out to build a recursive-language-model fabric and prove it runs. It did both. The strongest evidence is not the 44.4% — it is that the number exists at all: a cold boss under a cheap model, handed the fractality fabric and told to gate its work, actually delegated to workers that actually ran and actually returned results, through files on disk, under real pods, live. The design is sound. What remains is tuning (caps, menus, a couple of read verbs) and the deferred scope the owner parked: **Option C — the advisor slice (PP-003)**, next.

section.title: Next
section.p: **PP-003 — Option C, the advisor slice (D-C3-7):** research and execute it to completion (owner directive, 2026-07-12). Advisor = a worker-shaped run with an `advice` packet type, no ownership transfer; `advisor_enabled ⇐ caller_class ≥ medium`; uncertainty-triggered; accounting on the caller's budget.
